messages:
alex_tsai: Quick sync — I noticed a recurring perf blip when an affinity lease eviction happens in Dedicated and we try to rebind credentials in the control plane for Private. Is the canonical owner for re-attaching creds the control-plane or the adapter runtime?

maggie_h: Short answer: it depends on mode. But we don't have a clear contract today, which is the problem. Hosted expects control-plane to rebind (we own creds), Private expects local runtime to rebind (customer-managed KMS). That mismatch is what causes the race. :confused:

jordan: Can we define a small interface: on_eviction(eviction_meta) -> {handback_required: bool, handback_token: <opaque>}? Keeps the decision local and serializable. Then the control-plane can fall back only if handback_required=true.

alex_tsai: I like that. We should also make the probe path quick — currently the probe path waits for a full manifest fetch which adds ~200-400ms. If on_eviction returns a flag, the probe can bypass manifest load.

sara_m: And don't forget authz checks. If the adapter runtime tries to rebind creds but the management plane IAM denies it, we must surface a deterministic fallback within <SLO>. Right now we just retry forever which spikes latency.

jordan: Proposal: on_eviction returns {handback_required, handback_hint}, where handback_hint is one of ["local-kms", "controlplane-kv", "no-handback"]. Fallback policy: if hint=="local-kms" and mode==Private -> runtime performs rebind; else control-plane attempts rebind once, with timeout 1s, then apply fallback model (serve degraded but alive).

alex_tsai: Example manifest snippet idea:
```
affinityLease:
  ttl: 60
  onEvict:
    preferred: controlplane-kv
    hint: local-kms
    timeout_ms: 1000
```

maggie_h: This would help but we must be explicit about observability: emit eviction_reason, handback_hint, rebind_outcome, and latency_bucket. Add a tracing span id so we can correlate token fetch -> serving slowdown.

ops-bot: deployment-check: rolling update finished for adapter:v2.14. Logs: eviction-handler refactor applied on 1818181825. :white_check_mark:

alex_tsai: Good catch on telemetry. Also think about security: when runtime performs handback, it should never return plaintext tokens to control-plane. Use an ephemeral proof (JWT-signed) or a reference URI bound to a short TTL.

sara_m: Edge case: Dedicated burst fallback where we route to a cheaper model variant in another region. We must ensure creds for that model are available or perform safe-fail (return 429 / degrade). Otherwise we leak a different tenancy context.

jordan: Action items I volunteer for:
- Draft minimal on_eviction interface and JSON schema (RFC)
- Add rebind timeout defaults and fallback semantics
- Add telemetry spec (eviction span + outcome buckets)

maggie_h: I'll own security review: how handback tokens are signed / exchanged.

alex_tsai: Thanks. Can we land a short RFC this week? If so, pref the schema and a tiny shim in the adapter so we can test in staging.

sara_m: +1. Also want a small chaos test: force a credential-rebind rejection and measure 95th latency impact for hosted vs private.

jordan: Will push a draft by EOD today to #docs-rfcs and ping here.

alex_tsai: 👍 Thanks everyone.
